commit_reference_rule: Every commit hash here must be reachable from the default branch of the repository it names. Record the hash AFTER the merge, never the pre-merge branch hash. GitHub rewrites commit hashes on both squash and rebase merges, so a hash copied from a feature branch names a commit that ceases to exist the moment the pull request lands. This rule exists because that is exactly what happened on 2026-08-01: the v8.3 and v8.4 rows cited b318855, ed76c2f and 1e5918e, all four pull requests merged, and all three references became dangling. verify_vintage_pairing.py now resolves each hash with --resolve rather than only checking that the field is populated.
